newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Sept tourist trend down - ABS.
newsitem.headline: Australia Sept tourist trend down - ABS.

text.p: The number of foreign tourists visiting Australia dropped in trend terms in September for the first time in 10 months, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said on Monday.
But short-term arrivals for the first 10 months of the calendar year were 12.6 percent higher than in the same period in 1995, the bureau said.
"After 10 consecutive months of growth, the trend estimate for visitor arrivals showed a marginal decrease in September, 1996, at 354,300 compared to 354,400 for August, 1996," the bureau said.
The bureau said arrivals would have to increase 3.5 percent in October to achieve a zero growth in the trend estimate.
Total arrivals for January-September were 2.97 million, compared with 2.64 million in 1995, the bureau said.

The bureau said 60 percent of arrivals in that period said they were visiting Australia on holiday, 18 percent were visiting friends or relatives, 10 percent were on business and four percent travelled to Australia for education.
The net gain of permanent arrivals over departures to September was 83,000, 5.0 percent higher than the same period in 1995. -- Canberra bureau 61-6 273-2730
